title: Update docs URLs away from pkgs.rstudio.com
description:
Update pkgdown URL and cross-links as part of migrating away from pkgs.rstudio.com.

## Changes

- `pkgdown/_pkgdown.yml`: update `url` to `https://rstudio.github.io/ggcheck/`; update cross-link to gradethis docs
- `README.Rmd`, `README.md`, `man/fragments/readme-usage.Rmd`: update cross-links to gradethis docs

The ggcheck site already deploys to GitHub Pages — no CI changes needed.

A companion PR to `rstudio/pkgs.rstudio.com` will change the `pkgs.rstudio.com/ggcheck` proxy to a 301 redirect to the new URL.

title: Add `gradethis_equal()` method for `ggplot` objects
description:
`gradethis_equal.ggplot()` attempts to pass its inputs through `ggplot_build()` before comparing them. This computes all layer data for both plots, meaning there should no longer be spurious differences if one plot has been printed and the other has not.

``` r
library(ggplot2)
library(gradethis)
library(ggcheck)

plot_code <- quote(
  ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy, colour = class)) + 
    geom_point()
)

.result   <- eval(plot_code)
.solution <- eval(plot_code)

.result
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/wJE6yrG.png)<!-- -->

``` r

# Passes even if one plot has been printed
pass_if_equal()
#> <gradethis_graded: [Correct] Very good! Correct!>
```

<sup>Created on 2023-05-04 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

Closes rstudio/gradethis#345.

title: Allow `uses_mappings()` to find mappings that appear in every layer of the plot
description:
If `local_only = FALSE`, `get_mappings()` and `uses_mappings()` find mappings that appear in `ggplot()` _or_ in every layer of the plot

``` r
library(ggplot2)
library(ggcheck)

p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = mpg, group = cyl)) +
  geom_smooth(aes(y = mpg, group = am))

get_mappings(p, local_only = TRUE)
#> Aesthetic mapping: 
#> * `x` -> `wt`
get_mappings(p)
#> Aesthetic mapping: 
#> * `x` -> `wt`
#> * `y` -> `mpg`

uses_mappings(p, aes(x = wt, y = mpg), local_only = TRUE)
#> [1] FALSE
uses_mappings(p, aes(x = wt, y = mpg))
#> [1] TRUE

uses_mappings(p, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, group = cyl))
#> [1] FALSE
```

<sup>Created on 2022-03-17 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

Closes #34

title: Fix bug when `fail_if_not_ggplot()` attempts to access a `gradethis` `.result` object
description:
``` r
library(ggcheck)
library(ggplot2)
library(gradethis)

# Fails
grade_this({
  fail_if_not_ggplot()
})(mock_this_exercise(.user_code = "2"))
#> <gradethis_graded: [Incorrect]
#>   I expected your code to create a ggplot, but it created an object of
#>   class "numeric"
#> >


# Fails with special message
grade_this({
  fail_if_not_ggplot()
})(mock_this_exercise(.user_code = "geom_point()"))
#> <gradethis_graded: [Incorrect]
#>   I expected your code to create an entire ggplot, but it only created
#>   a ggplot layer (class "LayerInstance")
#> >

# Passes
grade_this({
  fail_if_not_ggplot()
})(mock_this_exercise(.user_code = "ggplot()"))
```

<sup>Created on 2022-02-24 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

Closes #32.

title: Add `is_ggplot()`
description:
Adds helper functions:
* `is_ggplot()` checks if an object is a `ggplot`.
* `stop_if_not_ggplot()` signals an error if an object is not a `ggplot`.
* `fail_if_not_ggplot()` returns a failing `gradethis` grade if an object is not a `ggplot`.

`stop_if_not_ggplot()` is now called before all functions that expect a `ggplot`.

``` r
library(ggcheck)
library(ggplot2)

p_valid <- ggplot(data = mpg, mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) +
  geom_point()
is_ggplot(p_valid)
#> [1] TRUE

p_invalid <- geom_point()
is_ggplot(p_invalid)
#> [1] FALSE

p_basic <- ggplot(data = mpg, mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy))
is_ggplot(p_basic)
#> [1] TRUE

stop_if_not_ggplot(p_valid) # No output
stop_if_not_ggplot(p_basic) # No output
stop_if_not_ggplot(p_invalid)
#> Error: `p` must be a "ggplot" object, not an object of class "LayerInstance"

# stop_if_not_ggplot() runs before all functions that expect a ggplot
uses_labels(p_invalid, x = "displ")
#> Error: `p` must be a "ggplot" object, not an object of class "LayerInstance"

fail_if_not_ggplot(p_valid) # No output
fail_if_not_ggplot(p_basic) # No output
fail_if_not_ggplot(p_invalid)
#> <gradethis_graded: [Incorrect]
#>   I expected your code to create a ggplot, but it created an object of
#>   class "LayerInstance"
#> >
```

<sup>Created on 2021-12-10 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

Closes #20.

title: Check for `aes` params in `uses_geom_param()`
description:
- Renames `uses_geom_param()` → `uses_geom_params()`, since it can check multiple params.
	- `uses_geom_param()` is preserved as an alias for backwards compatibility.
- Adds support for checking `aes` layer parameters with `uses_geom_params()`. You can now check for `geom`, `stat`, and `aes` layer parameters. 
- `params` can now be set by passing named arguments to `...`.
- `uses_geom_params()` now returns a named logical vector.
- Attempting to check an unset or invalid parameter now returns `FALSE` instead of an error.

``` r
library(ggcheck)
library(ggplot2)

p <- ggplot(mpg, aes(manufacturer)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "blue", color = "red", width = 0.5)

uses_geom_params(p, "bar", params = list(width = 0.5))
#> width 
#>  TRUE
uses_geom_params(p, "bar", params = list(fill = "blue"))
#> fill 
#> TRUE

uses_geom_params(p, "bar", width = 0.5, fill = "blue")
#> width  fill 
#>  TRUE  TRUE

# Unnamed arguments check if parameter is set
uses_geom_params(p, "bar", "fill", "color", "linetype")
#>     fill    color linetype 
#>     TRUE     TRUE    FALSE

# Support for color and colour
uses_geom_params(p, "bar", color = "red")
#> color 
#>  TRUE
uses_geom_params(p, "bar", colour = "red")
#> colour 
#>   TRUE

# Unset params return FALSE
uses_geom_params(p, "bar", linetype = "dashed")
#> linetype 
#>    FALSE
uses_geom_params(p, "bar", typo = TRUE)
#>  typo 
#> FALSE

# Alias for backwards compatibility
uses_geom_param(p, "bar", fill = "blue")
#> fill 
#> TRUE
```

<sup>Created on 2021-12-01 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

Closes #23 and #31.

title: Unnamed arguments to `uses_labels()` check if label is set
description:
You can now use unnamed arguments to `uses_labels()` to check if a a label for that aesthetic has been set.

``` r
library(ggcheck)
library(ggplot2)

p <- ggplot(data = mpg, mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(color = class, shape = drv)) +
  labs(x = "Weight", y = "MPG", color = NULL)

# Unnamed arguments check if a label is set for the given aesthetic
uses_labels(p, "x", "title")
#>     x title 
#>  TRUE FALSE

# The check will return TRUE for values set to NULL
uses_labels(p, "color")
#> color 
#>  TRUE

# The check will return TRUE if an aesthetic has a default label
uses_labels(p, "shape")
#> shape 
#>  TRUE

# You can check if a label has the default value with default_label()
uses_labels(p, color = default_label(), shape = default_label())
#> color shape 
#> FALSE  TRUE

# You can also use default_label() outside uses_labels() if you add arguments
default_label(p, c("x", "y"))
#> $x
#> [1] "displ"
#> 
#> $y
#> [1] "hwy"
```

<sup>Created on 2021-11-24 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

Closes #24.

title: Improve handling of `...` in `uses_labels()`
description:
This PR makes two major updates to `uses_labels()`:

- `uses_labels()` now returns a named logical vector instead of a single logical value

``` r
library(ggcheck)
library(ggplot2)

p <- ggplot(mpg, aes(x = displ, y = hwy, color = class)) +
  labs(x = "Weight", y = "MPG", color = NULL)

uses_labels(p, x = "Weight", y = "MPG", color = NULL)
#>     x     y color 
#>  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE
```

<sup>Created on 2021-11-23 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

- `uses_labels()` now splices lists of arguments, with or without the `!!!` operator

``` r
library(ggcheck)
library(ggplot2)

p <- ggplot(mpg, aes(x = displ, y = hwy, color = class)) +
  labs(x = "Weight", y = "MPG", color = NULL)

label_list <- list(y = "MPG", color = NULL)

uses_labels(p, x = "Weight", label_list)
#>     x     y color 
#>  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE

uses_labels(p, x = "Weight", !!!label_list)
#>     x     y color 
#>  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE
```

<sup>Created on 2021-11-23 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

Closes #25.

title: Add functions for checking plot labels
description:
Adds function `get_labels()` for listing (a subset of) the labels of a plot, and `uses_labels()` for checking if labels match their expected values.

``` r
library(ggcheck)
library(ggplot2)

p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, color = cyl)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = "weight", y = "MPG", color = NULL)

get_labels(p)
#> $x
#> [1] "weight"
#> 
#> $y
#> [1] "MPG"
#> 
#> $colour
#> NULL

get_labels(p, c("x", "y"))
#> $x
#> [1] "weight"
#> 
#> $y
#> [1] "MPG"

uses_labels(p, x = "weight")
#> [1] TRUE

uses_labels(p, color = NULL)
#> [1] TRUE

# If multiple arguments are given, returns TRUE only if all labels match
uses_labels(p, x = "weight", color = NULL)
#> [1] TRUE
```

<sup>Created on 2021-11-12 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

title: Check a geom or stat layer's parameters
description:
## Description

Instructors need to check that the student is using the right values for certain `geom_` or `stat_` functions when creating a layer (closes issue https://github.com/rstudio/ggcheck/issues/2). This PR supports that functionality and an enhancement to an existing functionality to get a specific layer.

## Changes:

- a `uses_geom_param` function that checks that a layer created with a `geom_` function is using the correct parameters
- a `uses_stat_param` function that checks that a layer created with a `stat_` function is using the correct parameters
- the `get_layer` function now includes a `stat` parameter (default `NULL`), which allows retrieval of layer by a stat suffix name
- added additional tests for added functionality

title: Core functionalities
description:
# Description
 
 This PR adds several core functionalities and makes a few improvements to existing ggcheck functions. It closes issues https://github.com/rstudio/ggcheck/issues/6 and https://github.com/rstudio/ggcheck/issues/7. 
 
 ## Layer checking
 
 - Added geom and stat lookup tables for mapping geom/stat function suffix to their appropriate geom/stat class name combination. Added getter functions to extract this information:
   - `map_geom` / `map_stat` to map a given geom/stat function suffix name to its proper ggplot2 geom/stat class name
   - `get_geoms_stats` / `ith_geoms_stats` to get a layer(s) geom/stat combinations
 - enhanced the `uses_geoms` function by adding an optional `stats` argument to check for geom + stat combinations
 - added `stats.R` mirroring `geoms.R` and adding a family of functions that check for the layer's stats
 
 ## Mappings checking
 
 - `identical_aes` function to compare two `aes` mappings uses `rlang::as_name` to strip environment
 - added a `uses_extra_mappings` function to check presence of extra aesthetic mappings in a plot
 - added a `uses_aesthetics` function to check presence of aesthetics (e.g. "x", "y") used in a plot
 
 ## Loose vs exact checking
 
 -  added an `exact` parameter as a flag to several checking functions to either use a loose sense of checking (presence) versus exact (identical to target properties including order)
 
 ## Tests
 
 - added additional tests for `geoms.R` for new functionality
 - added additional tests for `mappings.R` for new functionality
 - added tests for `stats.R`
 
 I have also tried to make documentation of functions clearer / consistent for family of geom/stat functions.
